messages:
Zoe: ACME reporting sustained 429s and high tail latency against their Dedicated pool starting ~2024-12-02T02:40Z. They say autoscaler is not bringing nodes up fast enough.
Zoe: I have their logs + a short timeline below, attaching what they sent.
Zoe: ```
[02:40:01] autoscaler: enqueue scale request desired=15 current=2 reason=probe_failures
[02:40:07] kubelet: image pull backoff registry.acme.corp/model-server:429
[02:40:12] init-sync: downloading shard=3 status=pending
[02:40:18] attach: auth=403 token refresh failure
[02:40:35] node gpux-12 io_wait=42%
```
Jorge: can you paste their dedicated config?
Zoe: ```yaml
dedicated:
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 40
  warmPool: 0
  probeTimeoutSeconds: 6
  attachRetries: 2
  initContainers:
    - name: model-sync
      image: registry.acme.corp/model-sync:stable
      resources: {cpu: 1, mem: 2Gi}
```
Sophia: this looks like a classic cold start + heavy init container + registry throttling combo. With warmPool=0 and minReplicas=1, a sudden surge will queue many attaches. If images are rate-limited and auth rotates, pods never become Ready and the autoscaler can't make progress.
Alex_oncall: triage checklist: 1) confirm imagePull backoff rates and 403/429 counts 2) check cloud node provisioning latency 3) inspect autoscaler rate-limit (maxScalePerMin) and queued scale request metrics.
Zoe: customer provided attach_latency metrics: P95=1.6s P99=3.9s and a spike of attach_failures at 02:40. I've requested a prometheus export.
Jorge: node io_wait 42% suggests disk/network contention — maybe multiple large model-syncs landing on same nodes. Any noisy-neighbor signals?
Sophia: I reproduced a similar pattern in a local test: many concurrent cold requests + model-sync init. Cloud node provisioning commonly took 70-100s which is the main contributor. Autoscaler enqueues, but if maxScalePerMin=3 you still ramp slowly.
Zoe: customer agreed to a short-term tweak: increase minReplicas to 5. They applied it at 02:55Z; 429s dropped sharply but P99 latency still ~2.1s.
Jorge: short-term support steps we should recommend: bump minReplicas, increase probeTimeoutSeconds to avoid marking pods failing during image pull, and consider warmPool=2 for peak windows.
Sophia: engineering notes: autoscaler should expose queued scale requests metric and the rate limiter state. Also consider a fast-ready hook for pods where only non-blocking init steps remain.
Alex_oncall: creating internal incident and paging runtime.
triage-bot: INC-54321 created, priority=P2, assigned_to=eng-runtime, runbook=dedicated-coldspin-scaleup
eng-runtime: acknowledged, will look at fast-ready and queued_scale metrics.
Jorge: infra to check registry quotas and request temporary burst allowance for ACME (ticket REG-802). Also verify nodepool parallel image pull limits.
Zoe: customer's short-term mitigation confirmed: minReplicas=5, probeTimeoutSeconds=20. They can't enable node pre-pull on their infra but will trial warmPool=2 during business hours tomorrow.
Sophia: one more point: check autoscaler config for maxScalePerMin — if it's small, even healthy nodes ready quickly won't eliminate the ramp. Logs showed several queued requests delayed by rate limiter.
Alex_oncall: support to follow up with ACME tomorrow 03:00Z with status and plan. Close when stable for 6 hours after changes.
customer-rep: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick response. We'll monitor and report any regressions. :thumbsup:
